explainBack.question: Why doesn't installing the Gemini Windows app mean Gemini can automatically read my screen, files or email?
explainBack.answer: Because the app is only a new route into the same cloud service — a second door into the same shop. Gemini only receives what you deliberately give it: text you paste, an image you choose to upload, or Google apps like Gmail and Drive that you explicitly connect. On a work or school account, an administrator additionally controls whether the app works at all. So access to your material is gated by your own choices and account controls, not by the fact that the software sits on your desktop.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: An accurate answer must use the route-not-tool mechanism (P004, P009), the opt-in upload/connection model (P006) and the admin gate (P005), without claiming any automatic screen or file access.
explainBack.assessment: The article supports this answer fully: P004 and P009 supply the causal frame, P006 the explicit-connection step, and P005 the account condition; the answer requires no facts outside the artifact.

unseenTransfer.scenario: Priya installs the Gemini Windows app on her employer-managed laptop. Alt + Space opens the window, but when she signs in with her work account it says Gemini isn't available. Her colleague, on a personal account, uses it fine and suggests Priya just connect her work Gmail to her personal Gemini to summarise a client thread.
unseenTransfer.question: Why is Priya blocked, and should she follow the colleague's workaround?
unseenTransfer.answer: She is blocked because on a managed work account the administrator controls whether Gemini is enabled; installing the app cannot override that (P005). The colleague's workaround is a bad idea: connecting apps is a deliberate data-sharing choice (P006, P008), and routing employer email through a personal account with no admin oversight shares work material she may not be entitled to share. The proportionate action is to ask her administrator whether Gemini is enabled, and until then use the app — if at all — only with material she is comfortable sharing under the right account.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: A correct solution applies the admin-gating mechanism from P005 and the choose-what-you-connect principle from P006/P008 to a situation the article never describes (a blocked managed sign-in and a risky workaround).
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism resolves this new scenario completely, including rejecting the workaround, so the transfer succeeds without invented facts.
